brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Four bases on one level: pieces at 0,0 / 1,-1 / 1,0 (full) and -1,1 (half-s), each with a top cover. The joints are bolted (lockJoints). End caps close every edge but one: a cap at 0,0 bearing 210 ran into the drawer frame, so that edge is open.
drawer:0#-1,1#cut sits on the cut face of the half base at -1,1.

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet, holding a small platform
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|1,-1|1,0 is a mount-type spike at the corner where bases 0,0, 1,-1 and 1,0 meet, carrying the platform-sm accessory. I moved the drawer to a different base because the first layout's drawer filled this corner (SPIKE_CLASH).

finish.summary: I built a compact desk unit from three full hex bases and one south-half base, all on a single level. A drawer sits in the half base. A mount spike with a small platform stands at the corner where the three full bases meet. All four bases have top covers, the joints are bolted, and the open edges have end caps except one: a cap there ran into the drawer frame, so that edge is open. The final check found no rule errors and no mesh collisions ("clear"). The build has 37 parts (about 1820 g of filament and 2638 min of printing). I added no props, since the brief didn't ask for any staging.

M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
